q: What happens to the APU Bleed when you select the APU BLD Pb?
a: The APU Bleed opens.

q: What does the Crossbleed Valve do when you select the APU BLD Pb?
a: The Crossbleed Valve opens.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What do the Engine Bleed Valves do when you select the APU BLD Pb?
a: The Engine Bleed Valves close.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: If the APU Bleed is left on during climb, at what altitude does it automatically close?
a: Passing 25,000 ft climbing.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: After closing automatically in the climb, at what altitude does the APU Bleed reopen in descent?
a: After descending through 23,000 ft.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: With the Crossbleed Valve in AUTO, Engines on and APU bleed OFF, what is the normal Crossbleed valve position?
a: Closed.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: When does the Crossbleed Valve move automatically?
a: Only when the APU BLD valve opens or closes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: When do we manually open or close the Crossbleed Valve?
a: Only when directed by ECAM.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What controls the Packs?
a: The Pack Controllers, one Pack Controller per pack.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: How many Pack Controllers are there per pack?
a: One Pack Controller per pack.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: If a Pack Controller fails, between what temperatures is the Pack outlet temperature regulated?
a: Between 48°F and 59°F.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What regulates the temperature in the aircraft?
a: The zone controller.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: How many zone controllers and channels are there?
a: One controller with two channels.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: If the zone controller fails, to what temperature is the aircraft regulated?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What does the Pack Flow Selector regulate?
a: The Pack Flow.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What pack flow does the LOW position of the Pack Flow Selector give?
a: 80% flow.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: In AUTO pack flow, where is the Passenger Count entered?
a: On the INIT A page in the MCDU.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: In AUTO pack flow, what is airflow automatically adjusted on?
a: The entered passenger load.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What pack flow does the HIGH position of the Pack Flow Selector give?
a: 120% flow.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: For what conditions is HIGH pack flow used?
a: Abnormally hot or humid conditions.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: When do the packs go to 125% flow?
a: When the APU Bleed is ON, or for Single Pack operations.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: Where is the HOT AIR system air tapped from?
a: Upstream of the packs.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: Which temperatures does the HOT AIR system regulate via the trim air valves?
a: Cockpit, Cabin, and FWD cargo temperatures.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What heats and what cools the Forward Cargo compartment?
a: Heated by Hot Air 1, cooled by Pack 2.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What primarily heats the Cockpit?
a: Hot Air 2.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: How are the valves in the Air Conditioning system controlled and operated?
a: All electrically controlled and pneumatically operated.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.3 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What temperature control range does the Flight Attendant CIDS panel have?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: On what is the Flight Attendant CIDS panel temperature range centered?
a: The Cabin temperature setting in the Cockpit.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: Where is the RAM AIR scoop located?
a: On the lower left side of the fuselage.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: In what failure case can the RAM AIR scoop provide air into the cabin?
a: Dual pack failure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: Which QRH checklist uses the RAM AIR scoop?
a: The Smoke/Fumes Removal Checklist.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: When will the RAM AIR Pb not function?
a: When the Ditching Pb is selected.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: At what ∆P will the RAM AIR system open?
a: When ∆P is less than 1 psi.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-10-10, DSC-36-10-30

q: What do the outflow valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on with the Press Mode Selector in AUTO?
a: They close.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What do the Cargo Isolation Valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
a: They close.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What does the Ram Air Inlet do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
a: It closes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What does the Avionics Ventilation Overboard Valve do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
a: It closes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What do the Pack Flow Control Valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
a: They close.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What are the two normal uses of the Ditching Pb?
a: Ditching, and Deicing (per FCOM Procedure).
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: Which cabin pressurization mode is the normal mode of operation?
a: AUTO.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: How many CPCs (Cabin Pressure Controllers) are there?
a: 2 CPCs.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: How many outflow valves are there, and how many motors does each use in AUTO mode?
a: 2 Outflow valves, each with 2 motors for the AUTO modes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: In AUTO mode, where does the pressurization system get the landing elevation?
a: FMGC provided landing elevation for the entered destination.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: When is the SEMI-AUTOMATIC pressurization mode used?
a: When operating at an airport not in the database.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: In SEMI-AUTOMATIC mode, how is the destination elevation set?
a: With the LDG ELEV selector.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: Which CPCs and motors does SEMI-AUTOMATIC mode use?
a: The same two CPCs and motors as the auto mode.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: In MANUAL pressurization mode, which controls are used to adjust pressurization?
a: MODE SEL to Manual, then VALVE SEL and V/S CTL per ECAM procedure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: In MANUAL pressurization mode, where are the target cabin altitudes provided?
a: In the FCOM and on the STS page.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: Which outflow valve motor is used for Manual mode?
a: A third motor on each Outflow valve.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: In MANUAL mode, how much change does each toggle of the V/S CTL give?
a: About 150-200 fpm.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.4 · DSC-21-20-10, DSC-21-20-40

q: What circulates the air that cools the avionics?
a: The Extract Fan.

q: On the ground, where is the avionics cooling air exhausted?
a: Out of the OVBD Extract Valve.

q: What happens to the OVBD Extract Valve and Underfloor Extract Valve at first engine start?
a: The OVBD Extract Valve closes and the Underfloor Extract Valve opens.

q: After first engine start, where does the avionics cooling air exit the aircraft?
a: Under the Forward Cargo compartment and out the Forward Outflow Valve.

q: What does the Underfloor Extract Valve do when the EXTRACT Pb is selected to OVRD?
a: It closes.

q: What does the OVBD Extract Valve do when the EXTRACT Pb is selected to OVRD?
a: It opens partially, using a separate small portion of the door.

q: Which ECAM procedures most likely call for selecting the EXTRACT Pb to OVRD?
a: Vent Extract Fault or Vent OVBD Valve Fault.

q: What is the source of air for the Cargo compartments?
a: Circulated Cabin air.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What is the top row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
a: Ventilation.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What is the middle row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
a: Cooling.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What is the bottom row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
a: Heating.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What happens to the Isolation Valves when a compartment Isolation Valve Pb is selected to Off?
a: The Inlet and Outlet Isolation Valves close.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What happens to the Extract Fan when a compartment Isolation Valve Pb is selected to Off?
a: The Extract Fan stops.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: With the Isolation Valve Pbs ON, when do the isolation valves automatically close?
a: When Cargo Smoke is detected or the Ditching Pb is selected ON.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What cools the forward cargo compartment?
a: Pack 2.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What heats the forward cargo compartment?
a: Hot Air 1.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What is the memory phrase for forward cargo heating and cooling?
a: Heated from the left, Cooled from the right.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What does the temperature selector knob below the cargo cooling selector control?
a: The trim air valve on the Hot Air 1 system.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: Can the Aft cargo compartment be heated or cooled?
a: No. It cannot be heated or cooled.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.5 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: How is the Bulk cargo compartment heated?
a: By an electric heater.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: When does the Bulk cargo compartment heater activate?
a: When the temperature falls below the set level.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What does the Bulk cargo heater do once the set temperature level is reached?
a: It shuts off until the temperature falls again.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What Bulk temperature do we set when live animals are carried in the Bulk compartment?
a: A comfortable temperature.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: What is the normal position of the FWD CARGO COOLING selector?
a: OFF, unless plants, livestock, or foods are carried.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: Which carried items require the FWD CARGO COOLING selector to be on?
a: Plants, Livestock, and Foods.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: In which compartment are pets carried?
a: The Bulk compartment.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.6 · DSC-21-40-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-06

q: Which QRH reset table is used to reset a blank or locked MCDU?
a: The QRH reset table (02.02D) and related procedures.

q: How can a blank or locked MCDU be turned off?
a: By pressing and holding the DIM key.

q: Which MCDU can be used as a replacement after a failed MCDU is turned off?
a: MCDU 3.

q: Below what altitude do the Autoland Lights become active in LAND mode?
a: Below 200 ft RA.

q: What is the action if the Autoland lights begin flashing?
a: Go Around.

q: When do mode reversions occur?
a: When the pilot asks the FMGEC to perform a task it is unable to do.

q: What does the FMGEC do during a mode reversion?
a: It reverts to a simpler mode to ensure a safe flight path.

q: What aural cue is heard when a mode reversion occurs?
a: A triple click, click click click, think Look Look Look.

q: During a managed climb in CLB and NAV, what does CLB revert to when HDG is selected?
a: OP CLB.

q: During a managed descent in DES and NAV, what does DES revert to when HDG is selected?
a: V/S.

q: When climbing or descending with ALT* engaged, what happens if a different altitude is selected?
a: ALT* reverts to V/S.

q: What happens when an altitude opposite to the direction of flight is set in the FCU?
a: The vertical mode reverts to V/S.

q: What does NAV revert to when overflying a route discontinuity?
a: HDG.

q: With the FDs on in a climb and the pilot leveling off without following them, to what speed does the aircraft accelerate?
a: Vmax.

q: In a climb with FDs on, what happens to the FDs and A/THR when Vmax is reached?
a: Both FDs disengage and A/THR reverts to SPEED.

q: In a climb with FDs on, what does A/THR do to thrust after reverting to SPEED at Vmax?
a: Reduces thrust to recover the speed target.

q: With the FDs on in a descent and the pilot leveling off without following them, to what speed does the aircraft decelerate?
a: Vls.

q: In a descent with FDs on, what happens to the FDs and A/THR when Vls is reached?
a: Both FDs disengage and A/THR reverts to SPEED.

q: In a descent with FDs on, what does A/THR do to thrust after reverting to SPEED at Vls?
a: Increases thrust to recover the speed target.

q: How many Autothrust computers and channels are there?
a: 1 Autothrust computer with 2 channels, one channel per FMGEC.

q: How is switching between Autothrust channels accomplished?
a: By switching autopilots.

q: What is the Match and Mash method of turning off the Autothrust inflight?
a: Match TLA on the EPR gauges to current thrust, then press the Instinctive Disconnect Pb.

q: What happens if the Instinctive Disconnect Pb is pressed and held for 15 seconds?
a: The Autothrust is removed for the remainder of the flight.

q: What protection is lost when the Autothrust is removed for the remainder of the flight?
a: Alpha Floor protection.

q: What is the Non-Standard method of turning off the Autothrust?
a: Retard the thrust levers to IDLE, then press the Autothrust Pb on the FCU.

q: What condition results from the Non-Standard method of turning off the Autothrust?
a: A Thrust Lock condition until the Thrust Levers are moved manually.

q: On takeoff, what arms the Autothrust?
a: Moving the Thrust Levers to Flex or TOGA.

q: What flashes on the FMA at THR RED altitude?
a: LVR CLB.

q: On takeoff, what activates the Autothrust?
a: Moving the Thrust Levers to CLB.

q: In flight, what activates the Autothrust?
a: Pressing the A/THR Pb.

q: After pressing the A/THR Pb in flight, how long does LVR CLB flash on the FMA?
a: Until the Thrust Levers are in the climb detent.

q: What is Groundspeed Mini designed to protect the aircraft from?
a: Windshear on approach.

q: What does Groundspeed Mini attempt to maintain during the approach?
a: A minimum energy level throughout the approach during variable wind conditions.

q: What must be engaged for Groundspeed Mini?
a: Managed speed.

q: Is Autothrust required for Groundspeed Mini?
a: No. Autothrust is not required.

q: What FMA is displayed on takeoff?
a: MAN FLEX __ | SRS | RWY | | A/THR.

q: When does RWY appear on the takeoff FMA?
a: Only if there is an ILS for that runway.

q: What color is A/THR on the takeoff FMA, and what does it signify?
a: Blue, meaning armed.

q: What FMA is displayed for an RNAV climb?
a: THR CLB | CLB | NAV | | A/THR.

q: What FMA is displayed in a vectored descent?
a: THR IDLE | OP DES | HDG | | A/THR.

q: What FMA is displayed in a NAV descent?
a: THR IDLE or THR DES | DES | NAV | | A/THR.

q: What FMA is displayed on an ILS APP?
a: SPEED | GS | LOC | CAT3/DUAL | 1AP2.

q: What is the highest landing capability of the aircraft?
a: CAT 3 DUAL.

q: What is the highest landing capability when single engine?
a: CAT 3 SINGLE.

q: What does 1 FD 2 on the FMA mean?
a: Normal mode of operation, both FDs selected on.

q: What does 1 FD on the FMA mean?
a: FD 2 is not selected on.

q: What does 1 FD 1 on the FMA mean?
a: FD 2 has failed.

q: What does SRS stand for?
a: Speed Reference System.

q: How does SRS deliver a speed?
a: It uses vertical guidance to deliver a speed.

q: What speed does SRS target on a normal takeoff?
What speed does SRS target on a go around?
a: The highest of Vapp or the current speed at Go Around.

q: What speed does SRS target single engine?
a: The highest of V2 or the airspeed at failure.

q: What must illuminate during a CVR test?
a: One or more green lights.

q: During preflight, to what position is the PA reception knob set?
a: The 12 o'clock position.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · PRO-NOR-SOP-06, DSC-23-10-50

q: Why is the PA reception knob set to the 12 o'clock position during preflight?
a: So the CVR records any PA transmissions.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · PRO-NOR-SOP-06, DSC-23-10-50

q: What can be used as a replacement if ACP 1 or ACP 2 fails?
a: ACP 3.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · PRO-NOR-SOP-06, DSC-23-10-50

q: Which control selects ACP 3 as a replacement for a failed ACP?
a: The AUDIO SWITCHING knob on the switching panel.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · PRO-NOR-SOP-06, DSC-23-10-50

q: What does the ALL call do?
a: CALL ALL CAPT appears on all FA panels.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · DSC-23-20-20, DSC 23-20-30

q: What does the MECH call activate?
a: A horn in the nose wheel well and a light on the external power panel.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · DSC-23-20-20, DSC 23-20-30

q: How long does the MECH call light remain illuminated?
a: Until reset by ground crew on the external power panel.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · DSC-23-20-20, DSC 23-20-30

q: What does the CAB REST call do?
a: Calls the Lower Crew Rest.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · DSC-23-20-20, DSC 23-20-30

q: What do the FWD, MID, EXIT and AFT calls do?
a: Call the associated FA station.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.9 · DSC-23-20-20, DSC 23-20-30

q: What does the EVAC switch activate?
a: The Evacuation Alert Audio.

q: Is the EVAC alert used per HAL procedure?
a: No. It is not used per HAL procedure.

q: During preflight, in what position do we verify the EVAC switch?
a: The CAPT position.

q: What does the EVAC switch in the CAPT position ensure?
a: The Flight Attendants cannot activate the Alert Audio.

q: Besides the cockpit switch, where is there an EVAC Pb?
a: On the forward CIDS panel.

q: How many lights are on the Cockpit Door Overhead Control Panel?
What does an illuminated light on the Cockpit Door Overhead Control Panel indicate?
a: The corresponding door latch is faulty.

q: What is the power hierarchy for AC BUS 1?
a: Generator 1, APU Generator, External B, External A, Generator 2.

q: What is the power hierarchy for AC BUS 2?
a: Generator 2, External A, APU Generator, External B, Generator 1.

q: Which source powers AC BUS 1 if Generator 1 is unavailable?
a: The APU Generator.

q: Which source powers AC BUS 2 if Generator 2 is unavailable?
a: External A.

q: When External A indicates AVAIL, what is powered regardless of the switch position?
a: The GND SRV Bus.

q: What happens when the External A Pb is selected ON?
a: External power connects to the rest of the system based on the power hierarchy.

q: What does the External B Pb display when selected with External B AVAIL?
a: AUTO.

q: Under what condition will External B connect with the system?
a: Provided the APU Generator is not online.

q: What does the AUTO indication on the External B Pb signify?
a: It connects and disconnects automatically based on the APU Generator status.

q: What normally powers the AC ESS BUS?
a: AC BUS 1.

q: If AC BUS 1 is lost, what powers the AC ESS BUS?
a: AC BUS 2 via the ESS XFEED.

q: What happens when ALTN is selected on the ESS XFEED Pb?
a: AC BUS 2 powers the AC ESS BUS.

q: During Initial Power Up, what should the battery voltage be above?
What battery charge does 25.5V represent?
a: 50% charge on the Batteries.

q: What do we do if the battery charge is lower than 25.5V at Initial Power Up?
a: Charge off external power for 20 minutes and check again.

q: Below what APU battery voltage is there a risk of an aborted APU start on battery only?
How do we check the battery voltages?
a: Select BAT 1, BAT 2, APU BAT Pbs off, read the Voltage Indicator window, switch batteries with the selector.

q: In what position is the battery selector left after checking battery voltages?
a: The APU BAT position.

q: What may not be available if the main batteries were low prior to an APU start on battery power?
a: The APU fire protection.

q: Which ECAM page is selected to check the Battery Charge Limiter during preflight?
a: The ELEC DC page.

q: What switching sequence is used to check the Battery Charge Limiter?
a: Turn off BAT 1, BAT 2, and APU BAT, then turn them back on.

q: What battery draw verifies the Battery Charge Limiter is functioning properly?
a: Less than 60 amps in 10 seconds or less.

q: How long can we operate on batteries only?
a: A minimum of 30 minutes.

q: What does the GALLEY Pb AUTO position (lights out) indicate?
a: The galley will automatically shed in case of failures.

q: What does the COMMERCIAL Pb control?
a: Everything back of the Cockpit door (Galley, IFE, Cargo loading, etc.).

q: How long, at most, should the IDG disconnect be held?
a: Not greater than 3 seconds.

q: Why should the IDG disconnect not be held for greater than 3 seconds?
a: The disconnect mechanism could be damaged.

q: Can the IDG be reconnected in flight?
a: No. The IDG cannot be reconnected in flight.

q: Which items connect to the Hot Battery bus on the ground and remain powered at all times?
a: The Clock and the Battery Voltage Indication Window.

q: What is the EMER GEN TEST used for?
a: A maintenance function only.

q: What does the EMER ELEC PWR panel label refer to?
a: The Emergency Generator.

q: Where is the EMER ELEC CONFIG summary located?
a: In the QRH.

q: What is powering the aircraft when it is in EMER ELEC CONFIG?
a: The Emergency Generator, with many electrical items shed.

q: Which hydraulic system powers the Emergency Generator?
a: The green hydraulic system, via two methods.

q: What powers the green system in the “Big Green” case?
a: One or both engine driven pumps.

q: What powers the green system in the “Little Green” case?
a: The RAT only.

q: What percentage of an engine driven pump flow capability can the RAT provide?
a: Between 15% and 45%, depending on airspeed.

q: Loss of which two busses automatically activates EMER ELEC CONFIG?
a: AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2, with both Engine Generators tripped offline.

q: After loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2, what powers the Emergency Generator?
a: Big Green hydraulics.

q: How many busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
a: 4 busses.

q: Which 4 busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
a: AC ESS, AC ESS SHED, DC ESS, DC ESS SHED.

q: Which displays remain in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
a: Captains PFD, Captains ND, and E/WD.

q: After loss of both engines, what powers the Emergency Generator?
a: Little Green (the RAT only).

q: How many busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
a: 2 busses.

q: Which 2 busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
a: AC ESS and DC ESS.

q: Which displays remain in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
a: Captains PFD and E/WD.

q: Can the emergency generator be turned on manually?
a: Yes. It can also be manually turned on.

q: Once the emergency generator has been turned on, can it be turned off?
a: No. It cannot be turned off.

q: When does a RAT-powered emergency generator disconnect?
a: When the slats are extended.

q: How is the RAT-powered emergency generator reactivated after slat extension disconnects it?
a: Push the MAN ON Pb after the slats have been retracted.

q: Below what airspeed does the RAT stop being effective?
a: Less than 140 kts.

q: What is the only source of power once the RAT stops being effective below 140 kts?
a: The batteries.

q: What happens to the Land Recovery AC and DC busses when the aircraft enters EMER ELEC CONFIG?
a: They shed.

q: What kind of systems are on the Land Recovery busses?
a: Systems required for landing but not during cruise.

q: Do the Land Recovery busses recover automatically if normal power is restored?
a: No. They remain shed even if normal power is restored.

q: What does the Land Recovery Pb do?
a: Recovers the Land Recovery AC and DC busses, restoring systems required for landing.

q: Which systems does the Land Recovery Pb restore when Big Green powers the Emergency Generator?
a: LGCIU 1, SFCC 1, BSCU CH 1, LH Windshield Heat, LH Landing Light.

q: Which systems does the Land Recovery Pb restore when Little Green powers the Emergency Generator?
a: LGCIU 1 and SFCC 1 (slat channel only).

q: Are the reset panel switches circuit breakers?
a: No. They are computer reset switches.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: Where is the explanation of the reset procedures found?
a: The first page of the reset sections in both the FCOM and QRH.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: When can you accomplish a computer reset as directed?
a: When instructed by an ECAM or paper QRH procedure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: If no ECAM or QRH procedure directs a reset, how do you determine whether one is allowed?
a: Check the QRH table.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: How are system Pbs that also function as resets marked?
a: Noted by /R.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: Which two cockpit switches are also resets?
a: The MCDU and A/SKID & N/W STRG (BSCU) switches.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: How many circuit breakers are in the cockpit?
a: Only 5.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.13 · PRO-ABN-ABN-RST, QRH 02.02

q: Where are the 5 cockpit circuit breakers located?
a: 3 on the cockpit door frame, 1 under each pilot seat on the pedestal.

q: With the Emergency Exit Light switch armed, what conditions bring the lights on?
a: Normal electrical power fails, DC ESS Bus fails, AC BUS 1 fails, or cabin altitude over 9550 ft.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-33-30-20, DSC-33-40-10

q: Which emergency lights come on when AC BUS 1 fails with the exit lights armed?
a: Only the overhead emergency lights, to provide minimum lighting.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-33-30-20, DSC-33-40-10

q: At what cabin altitude do the EXIT signs come on with the exit lights armed?
a: Over 9550 ft.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-33-30-20, DSC-33-40-10

q: When are the Fasten Seat Belt signs on in the Auto position?
a: When either the gear is extended, or the flaps/slats are not at 0.

q: Why are the No Smoking lights always on?
a: They are hardwired.

q: What else comes on when the No Smoking switch is in the ON position?
a: The EXIT signs.

q: What happens if the No Smoking switch is left ON after all power is shut off?
a: The EXIT sign internal batteries would be depleted. Turned off in the Securing Checklist.

q: What is the No Smoking switch used to signal to the Flight Attendants?
a: Passing through 10000 ft.

q: What type of fire detection loops do the engines use?
a: Gas detection loops, the same as the APU.

q: How many gas filled fire detection loops does each engine have?
a: 2 loops.

q: How does a gas filled fire detection loop sense a fire?
a: Heated gas expands and sets off a sensor at a predetermined level.

q: Is an engine fire warning issued when both loops detect a fire?
a: Yes. Both loops detecting a fire issues a warning.

q: Is an engine fire warning issued when one loop detects a fire and the other is inoperative?
a: Yes. One loop detecting fire with the other inoperative issues a warning.

q: Within what time must both engine loops break to issue a fire warning?
a: Within 5 seconds of each other.

q: What happens to the engine fire warnings if the fire goes out?
a: The warnings stop.

q: How many Halon bottles are there per engine?
a: 2 Halon bottles per engine.

q: What happens to the CRC when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: It is silenced.

q: What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the FADEC?
a: Removes power from the FADEC.

q: What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the SQUIBS?
a: Arms the SQUIBS.

q: Which hydraulic and fuel valves close when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The Hydraulic Fire Shutoff Valve and the Low-Pressure Fuel Valve.

q: What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the IDG?
a: Deactivates the IDG.

q: Which pneumatic valves close when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The Pack Flow Control Valve and the Engine Bleed Valve.

q: What aural and master warning indications occur during the Engine Fire Test?
a: The CRC sounds and the Master Warning lights flash.

q: Which Pb lights come on during the Engine Fire Test?
a: The Engine Fire Pbs and the SQUIB and DISCH lights.

q: Where do fire lights come on near the pedestal during the Engine Fire Test?
a: By the Engine Master Switches.

q: How does the ENG 1 FIRE ECAM presentation differ from ENG 2 FIRE during the Engine Fire Test?
a: ENG 1 FIRE appears on the left with checklist, ENG 2 FIRE on the right as title only.

q: How many lights in total illuminate during the Engine Fire Test?
a: 12 lights (including 2 ECAM messages), plus the CRC.

q: What controls the automatic functions of the APU?
a: The ECB (Electronic Control Box).

q: What happens automatically in case of an APU fire on the ground?
a: APU shutdown and fire extinguishing.

q: Does automatic APU shutdown and fire extinguishing occur if the APU fire happens airborne?
a: No. It will not happen airborne.

q: How many Halon bottles does the APU have?
a: 1 Halon bottle.

q: How many gas filled fire detection loops does the APU have?
a: 2 loops.

q: Under what three conditions is an APU fire warning issued?
a: Both loops detect fire, one detects with the other inoperative, or both break within 5 seconds.

q: What happens to the APU fire warnings if the fire goes out?
a: The warnings stop.

q: What happens to the APU itself when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The APU shuts down.

q: What happens to the CRC and squib when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The CRC is silenced and the squib is armed.

q: Which fuel items are affected when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The LP Fuel Valve closes and the APU Fuel Pumps (FWD and AFT) shut off.

q: What happens to the APU generator when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: It deactivates.

q: Which pneumatic valves close when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
a: The APU bleed valve and the Crossbleed valve.

q: Which lights and messages appear when the APU fire test Pb is pushed?
a: APU FIRE Pb, AGENT SQUIB and DISCH Pb lights, 2 Master Warnings, CRC, E/WD APU FIRE message.

q: How many Master Warning lights illuminate during the APU fire test?
a: 2 Master Warning lights.

q: What is the total item count by color during the APU fire test?
a: 4 red lights/messages, 1 amber light, 1 white light, and the CRC.

q: What type of detectors does Avionics Smoke detection use?
a: Optical Particle Detectors.

q: What type of smoke detectors does the Cargo Smoke system use?
a: Optical detectors.

q: Why is it not possible to tell if a cargo fire has been extinguished?
a: Remaining particulates and Halon in the compartment keep the optical detectors sensing.

q: How many Halon bottles does the cargo fire extinguishing system have?
a: 2 bottles, both discharging into the selected compartment.

q: How quickly does the first cargo Halon bottle discharge?
a: Within 60 seconds.

q: How is the second cargo Halon bottle released?
a: Through a restrictor valve.

q: How long does the second cargo Halon bottle take to fully discharge?
a: 260 minutes.

q: Why does the second cargo Halon bottle discharge over 260 minutes?
a: For ETOPS requirements (195 minutes).

q: When does the cargo bottle DISCH light illuminate?
a: Not until the bottle is fully empty.

q: Which Pb controls cargo fire extinguishing for the Bulk compartment?
a: The Aft Pb. The bottles discharge into both the Aft and Bulk compartments.

q: What is the cargo smoke Test button used for?
a: A maintenance function only.

q: How many PRIMs does the aircraft have?
a: 3 PRIMs, used for Normal, Alternate, and Direct Laws.

q: How many SECs does the aircraft have?
a: 2 SECs, used for Direct Law if no PRIMs are working.

q: Which flight control law do the SECs provide if no PRIMs are working?
a: Direct Law.

q: Are the FCC Pbs reset switches?
a: Yes. All FCC Pbs are reset switches.

q: How many flight control computers are needed to perform a safe landing?
a: Only 1 computer of any type.

q: On which SD page are the speedbrakes displayed?
a: The F/CTL page.

q: Which spoiler panels are used for speedbrakes and ground spoilers?
a: All the panels. Only some are used for roll control.

q: Can the speedbrakes be used with Full flaps?
a: Yes. The speedbrakes can be used with Full flaps.

q: Can the aircraft be landed with the speedbrakes extended?
a: Yes. The aircraft can be landed with the speedbrakes extended.

q: During an RTO, what conditions cause the ground spoilers to extend?
a: Thrust levers retarded to idle with speed greater than 72 kts.

q: When armed, what causes the ground spoilers to extend during landing?
a: Main gear compression with the thrust levers at IDLE.

q: When not armed, what causes the ground spoilers to extend during landing?
a: Main gear compression with at least 1 engine in reverse.

q: What do the ground spoilers do if only 1 main gear touches down with reverse selected on 1 engine?
a: They partially extend until the second main gear touches down, then extend normally.

q: Why do the ground spoilers only partially extend when one main gear touches down first?
a: It allows a smoother touchdown in crosswind conditions.

q: When can the rudder trim be manually adjusted?
a: Only when the autopilot is off.

q: What happens to the rudder trim knob and reset button when the autopilot is on?
a: They do not function.

q: Which computers control the TURB DAMP function?
a: The PRIMs.

q: What does the TURB DAMP function do?
a: Dampens structural modes induced by atmospheric turbulence.

q: When can TURB DAMP be turned off?
a: If it is considered not to be helping comfort.

q: What three parameters must be met for TURB DAMP to be active?
a: In flight within normal envelope, Normal Law active or A/P engaged, airspeed greater than 200 kts.

q: Above what airspeed is TURB DAMP active?
a: Greater than 200 kts.

q: How many pilots should make sidestick inputs at a time?
a: Only one pilot.

q: What happens to the inputs when both sidesticks are moved at the same time?
a: The inputs are summed.

q: What audio warning sounds when both sidesticks receive inputs at the same time?
a: “Dual Input”.

q: Which SIDE STICK PRIORITY lights illuminate during a dual input?
a: Green “CAPT” and “FO” lights.

q: How does a pilot take control of the sidesticks from the other pilot?
a: Press and hold the red Pb on their sidestick.

q: When both pilots press and hold their sidestick red Pb, who has priority?
a: The last pilot to press and hold.

q: For which pilot does the red arrow in the SIDE STICK PRIORITY light illuminate?
a: The pilot who is no longer in control.

q: What audio message accompanies a sidestick priority takeover?
a: “Priority Left” or “Priority Right” as appropriate.

q: How long must the red Pb be held to lock out the other pilot's sidestick for the remainder of the flight?
a: More than 40 seconds.

q: How can a deactivated sidestick be activated again?
a: Push its red Pb.

q: What does the green band on the THS wheel indicate?
a: The certified limits.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.17 · DSC-27-20-30, FCTM AS-CG

q: What does setting the pitch trim within the THS green band ensure?
a: The aircraft can perform a safe takeoff.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.17 · DSC-27-20-30, FCTM AS-CG

q: What does having the correct pitch trim setting provide?
a: A consistent rotation.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.17 · DSC-27-20-30, FCTM AS-CG

q: When is the Automatic Retraction System (ARS) used?
a: Heavy weight operations when S speed is greater than or near the 1+F limit speed of 215 kts.

q: At what speed does the ARS automatically retract the flaps?
a: As the speed increases through 200 kts.

q: What does the Flap Load Relief System do?
a: Automatically retracts the flaps to the next retracted lever position in an overspeed.

q: In Flaps 2, 3, or FULL, how much overspeed causes the flaps to retract one position?
a: 2.5 kts overspeed.

q: What is displayed on the PFD when the Flap Load Relief System is active?
a: RELIEF, above the Slat/Flap indicator.

q: When do the flaps reextend after a flap load relief retraction?
a: After the aircraft slows to 2.5 kts below Vfe.

q: What does the Alpha/Speed Lock inhibit?
a: Slat retraction from 1 to 0.

q: What speed or Alpha conditions activate the Alpha/Speed Lock?
a: Speed below 148 kts or Alpha exceeding 8.5 degrees.

q: What is displayed on the PFD when the Alpha/Speed Lock is active?
a: LOCK, above the Slats/Flaps indicator.

q: What conditions allow the slats to retract to 0 after an Alpha/Speed Lock?
a: Alpha below 8.2 degrees and speed exceeding 154 kts.

q: Why do the ailerons droop when the flaps are set at 1 or greater?
a: To provide additional lift.

q: How much do the ailerons droop at Flaps 1+F?
a: 5 degrees.

q: How much do the ailerons droop at Flaps 2 through Full?
a: 10 degrees.

q: Is there aileron droop when Flaps 1 is selected while airborne?
a: No. No flaps are extended at Flaps 1 airborne, so there is no droop.

q: How many Fuel Control and Monitoring Computers (FCMC) control the fuel system?
a: 2 FCMCs.

q: What is the approximate capacity of each outer tank?
a: Approximately 6,300 lbs each.

q: What is the approximate capacity of each inner tank?
a: Approximately 72,000 lbs each.

q: What is the approximate capacity of the tail tank?
a: Approximately 11,000 lbs.

q: What is the approximate capacity of the center tank?
a: Approximately 72,000 lbs.

q: What is the approximate total fuel capacity?
a: Approximately 240,000 lbs.

q: Which tanks fill first during refueling?
a: The Inners and Outers.

q: At around what total fuel load should fuel start going into the Trim tank?
a: Around 80,500 lbs.

q: At around what total fuel load should fuel start going into the Center tank?
a: Around 163,000 lbs.

q: From where do the engines draw their fuel?
a: The INNER tank collector cells.

q: In what order do the other tanks feed the INNER tank as fuel burns off?
a: CENTER to INNER, then TRIM to INNER, then OUTER to INNER.

q: What is the tail trim tank used for?
a: CG control during flight.

q: Why is the CG moved aft during cruise?
a: For optimum aircraft performance.

q: What effect does an aft CG have during takeoff?
a: It reduces stability.

q: Passing what flight level in the climb do the FCMCs start the aft transfer to the trim tank?
During cruise, why is trim tank fuel transferred forward as needed?
a: To maintain Inner tank levels and optimum CG.

q: When do the FCMCs begin the forward transfer of remaining trim tank fuel during descent?
a: Passing FL 24.5, or when 35 minutes or less from destination.

q: What does selecting FWD on the TTANK MODE Pb do?
a: Manually transfers fuel from the TRIM tank to the CENTER tank.

q: Which is the only fuel transfer Pb with a direction?
a: TTANK MODE (FWD).

q: What happens with the TTANK Feed switch in the AUTO position?
a: The FCMC automatically transfers fuel throughout the flight.

q: Why is the final forward transfer stopped with a small amount of fuel left in the trim tank?
a: So the trim tank transfer line contains fuel for APU operation.

q: What does the OPEN position of the TTANK Feed switch do?
a: Opens the valves to allow gravity feed to the center tank.

q: What happens to the trim tank transfer line with the TTANK Feed switch in OPEN?
a: It is drained, and the APU will not operate.

q: What does the ISOL position of the TTANK Feed switch do?
a: Stops all transfers.

q: What does the CTR TANK XFR Pb do?
a: Performs a manual transfer from the Center tank to the Inner tanks.

q: How much fuel is unusable if the Center tank pumps are inoperative?
Why is 33,000 lbs of center tank fuel unusable with the Center tank pumps inoperative?
a: Due to gravity and wing dihedral.

q: What does the OUTR TK XFR Pb do?
a: Performs a gravity transfer from the Outer tanks to the Inner tanks by opening the valves.

q: Can the engines suction feed fuel?
a: Yes. They can suction feed from the collector tanks.

q: What should be used to conduct all manual fuel transfers?
a: The ECAM/QRH procedures.

q: What protection is lost during manual fuel transfers?
a: Overfill protections. Tanks could overfill and fuel could be lost overboard.

q: When does the WING XFEED open automatically?
a: During a fuel jettison and during EMER ELEC CONFIG.

q: At around what fuel imbalance should you start checking the limitations chart?
a: Around 3,200 lbs imbalance.

q: At what fuel imbalance does the advisory come on?
a: 6,600 lbs imbalance.

q: Can the aircraft be flown and landed in any fuel imbalance scenario?
a: Yes. In exceptional conditions, in any fuel imbalance scenario.

q: What do the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons do?
a: Close a valve in each Inner tank, closing the connection between the 2 parts of the tank.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: What is the normal position of the inner tank split valve?
a: Open.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: What is the purpose of splitting the inner tank?
a: To protect a portion of the inner tank fuel in case of a fuel leak.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: After an inner tank split, is all fuel still accessible?
a: Yes. All fuel is still accessible via the main and standby pumps.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: Why are the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons not on the main fuel panel?
a: They were added after initial design.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: Are the INR TANK SPLIT valves monitored by ECAM?
a: No. They were added after initial design and are not monitored by ECAM.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: When are the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons used?
a: Only when directed by ECAM.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: What does the amber ON light on an INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton indicate?
a: The valve is closing.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: What does the blue SHUT light on an INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton indicate?
a: The valve is shut.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: Which INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton lights are illuminated once the tank is split?
a: Both the amber ON and blue SHUT lights.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.19 · DSC-28-10-20, DSC-28-20

q: What is the fuel jettison rate?
a: 2200 lbs/min plus fuel burn.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: What happens to the fuel pumps once the jettison QRH procedure is accomplished?
a: All fuel pumps turn on.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: What does the crossfeed valve do when jettison begins?
a: It opens.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: Which valves open to begin fuel jettison?
a: The jettison valves.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: Which fuel transfers begin during jettison?
a: Trim tank to Center tank, and Outer tanks to Inner tanks.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: From which tanks is fuel jettisoned?
a: Both the Inner tanks and the Center tank simultaneously.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: How does the crew stop a fuel jettison?
a: Using the QRH procedure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: Which MCDU page entry stops the jettison automatically when reached?
a: The fuel level input into the MCDU FUEL PRED page.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: At what combined Inner tank fuel quantity does jettison stop?
a: 22,000 lbs combined Inner tank fuel quantity.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: Which low level sensor condition stops the jettison?
a: Both inner tank low level sensors on one side go dry.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: How many conditions stop a fuel jettison?
a: Four: crew QRH stop, MCDU FUEL PRED level reached, combined Inner 22,000 lbs, one side's low level sensors dry.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.20 · DSC-28-10-120, QRH 19.02A

q: How many Hydraulic System Monitoring Units (HSMU) control the hydraulic system?
a: 1 HSMU.

q: Where is the Hydraulic Architecture diagram found?
a: In the QRH, OPS.08A.

q: What are the 3 independent hydraulic systems?
a: Green, Blue, Yellow.

q: Can hydraulic fluid be transferred between the systems?
a: No. Fluid cannot be transferred between the systems.

q: What is normal hydraulic pressure?
What hydraulic pressure does the RAT provide?
Which is the main hydraulic system?
a: Green.

q: What powers the Green hydraulic system?
a: 2 Engine Driven pumps plus the Ram Air Turbine (RAT).

q: What is the Green system Priority Valve designed to do?
a: Prioritize the flight controls in a low-pressure situation.

q: Which high draw items does the Green Priority Valve cut off in low pressure?
a: Emergency Generator, Nosewheel Steering, Landing Gear.

q: What does the white tick mark on the SD HYD page Green reservoir signify?
a: Fluid is above 17 L / 4.5 USG.

q: What happens to the Green reservoir white tick mark if fluid falls below 17 L?
a: It becomes two amber bars.

q: Which notable brake items are on the Blue hydraulic system?
a: Alternate Brakes, Parking Brake, Brake Accumulator.

q: Which hydraulic system operates the Cargo Doors?
a: Yellow.

q: Which hydraulic systems power parts of the flight controls?
a: All three: Green, Blue and Yellow.

q: What pumps does each hydraulic system have?
a: An Engine driven pump and an Electric Pump. Green has 2 Engine Driven Pumps.

q: How many Engine Driven Pumps does the Green system have?
How long are the hydraulic electric pumps intended to be used?
a: Temporary use only.

q: Can the electric pumps replace the Engine driven pumps?
a: No. They are for temporary use only.

q: How many Pbs control each hydraulic electric pump?
a: Two Pbs.

q: What does the top electric pump Pb select?
a: AUTO/STBY or ON.

q: What does the bottom electric pump Pb do?
a: Turns the pump off.

q: How is an electric pump that was manually selected ON turned off?
a: By returning the top Pb to AUTO.

q: When should the bottom electric pump Pb OFF position be used?
a: Only if directed by ECAM/QRH/FCOM.

q: When does the Green electric pump come on automatically?
a: When either engine has failed, or when the gear has been selected up.

q: How long does the Green electric pump run after the gear is selected up?
a: 25 seconds, to ensure gear retraction within the proper time.

q: When does the Blue electric pump come on automatically?
a: Engine 1 has failed and PRIM 1 or PRIM 3 is also inoperative.

q: Why does the Blue electric pump run with Engine 1 failed and PRIM 1 or 3 inoperative?
a: To assist rudder authority by ensuring at least 2 actuators are operating the rudder.

q: When does the Yellow electric pump come on after an engine failure?
a: Engine 2 has failed and the flap lever is not at 0.

q: Why does the Yellow electric pump run after Engine 2 fails with the flap lever not at 0?
a: To ensure flap retraction within the proper time.

q: What happens to the Yellow electric pump when the Green electric pump runs for gear retraction after Engine 2 failure?
a: It shuts off until the Green electric pump turns off.

q: After Engine 2 failure, how long does the Yellow electric pump stay running?
a: Until engine shutdown.

q: Besides Engine 2 failure, when does the Yellow electric pump turn on automatically?
a: During cargo door operation (Blue ON light illuminates automatically).

q: Which valve also turns on during cargo door operation?
a: The Yellow Leak Measurement Valve.

q: What does the Ram Air Turbine provide?
a: Redundancy to Green, backup hydraulic power to the flight controls and/or the emergency generator.

q: Which engine condition automatically deploys the RAT?
a: Engines 1 and 2 fail.

q: Which Green and Blue condition automatically deploys the RAT?
a: Green and Blue Fluid Low Level.

q: Which Green and Yellow condition automatically deploys the RAT?
a: Green and Yellow Fluid Low Level.

q: Can the RAT be manually deployed?
a: Yes. The RAT can also be manually deployed.

q: Who can stow the RAT?
a: Only maintenance, on the ground.

q: What is the minimum RAT speed?
a: 140 kts.

q: What are the Leak Measurement Valves used for?
a: To isolate the flight controls from hydraulic pressure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: When does the yellow Leak Measurement Valve operate automatically?
a: When the Yellow hydraulic pump activates during cargo door operation.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: What is the normal mode for PROBE/WINDOW HEAT?
a: AUTO.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: When are probes and windows automatically heated?
a: In flight, and on the ground with at least one engine running.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: Which probe is not heated on the ground?
a: The TAT probe.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What does selecting the PROBE/WINDOW HEAT Pb to ON do?
a: Activates Probe/Window heat, except the TAT probes on the ground.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: How does probe/window heat level differ between ground and flight?
a: Low heat on the ground, high heat in flight.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: When is ENG ANTI ICE selected on?
a: When expecting potential icing. It is used as an anti-ice system.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: How do the Engine Anti Ice valves fail with an electrical failure?
a: Open.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What limitations apply to the use of Engine Anti Ice?
a: None.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What happens to EPR when Engine Anti Ice is selected on?
a: The EPR limit is reduced and the EPR idle is increased.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: Does engine ignition automatically come on when Engine Anti Ice is selected on?
a: No. Only if there was an EIU failure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: Below what SAT is Engine Anti Ice not required in climb or cruise?
a: Below -40C SAT, due to the cold temperature.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.22 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: When is WING ANTI ICE turned on?
a: Only when instructed by the ECAM or when there is visible ice buildup. It is a deice system.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.23 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: Which slats are heated by WING ANTI ICE?
a: Only the outer 4 slats.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.23 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: How do the WING ANTI ICE valves fail with an electrical failure?
a: Closed, because hot air with no cooling airflow can damage the wing composite.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.23 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What happens when WING ANTI ICE is activated on the ground?
a: A 30 second test occurs, then the valves close until after liftoff.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.23 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What happens to EPR when WING ANTI ICE is selected on?
a: The EPR limit is reduced and the EPR idle is increased.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.23 · DSC-30-10-10, PRO-NOR-SUP-ADVWXR

q: What does one push of the RAIN RPLNT button do?
a: Distributes a measured quantity of fluid to the associated side.

q: When must rain repellent not be used?
a: On a dry windshield.

q: What is the maximum wiper operating speed?
a: 230 kts.

q: What type of items are Level 3 ECAM Warnings?
a: Immediate action items.

q: What alerts accompany a Level 3 ECAM Warning?
a: CRC sounds, Master Warning lights flash, message in red text on the E/WD.

q: What type of items are Level 2 ECAM Cautions?
a: Crew awareness items not requiring immediate action.

q: What alerts accompany a Level 2 ECAM Caution?
a: A single chime, Master Caution lights on, message in amber text on the E/WD.

q: What type of items are Level 1 ECAM Cautions?
a: Crew monitoring items.

q: What alerts accompany a Level 1 Caution for loss of redundancy?
a: No aural alerts, no Master Caution lights, message in amber text on the E/WD.

q: How does an ECAM Advisory present on the SD?
a: The relevant system page is called with the affected parameter pulsing green.

q: What could an ECAM Advisory indicate?
a: An impending failure. The system requires crew monitoring.

q: Which QRH chart is referenced for an ECAM Advisory?
a: The ECAM Advisory Conditions Chart, QRH 01.01A.

q: What is Groundspeed Mini designed to protect the aircraft from?
a: Windshear on approach, by maintaining a minimum energy level in variable wind conditions.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-22-30-90, DSC-31-40

q: Which speed mode must be engaged for Groundspeed Mini?
a: Managed speed.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-22-30-90, DSC-31-40

q: Is Autothrust required for Groundspeed Mini?
a: No.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-22-30-90, DSC-31-40

q: What do the amber double tick marks on the PFD speed tape represent?
a: VFE Next.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-22-30-90, DSC-31-40

q: What does a blank tuning letter next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
a: The NAVAID is autotuned.

q: What does the letter M next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
a: Manually tuned in the RADNAV page of the MCDU.

q: What does the letter R next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
a: Physically tuned in the RMP.

q: Does manually tuning a NAVAID affect the autotuning functions?
a: No.

q: Why does the ECAM inhibit some warnings and cautions during takeoff?
a: To avoid unnecessary distraction.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-31-15, PRO-NOR-SOP-07

q: When does the takeoff ECAM inhibit apply?
a: From takeoff thrust until 1500 ft or 2 minutes after liftoff.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-31-15, PRO-NOR-SOP-07

q: What happens to inhibited alerts once above 1500 ft or 2 minutes after liftoff?
a: The inhibit is lifted and any inhibited alerts are displayed.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-31-15, PRO-NOR-SOP-07

q: Which E/WD message must be displayed for pushback?
a: N/WS DISC.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-31-15, PRO-NOR-SOP-07

q: What if N/WS DISC is not displayed but the ground crew says the pin is in?
a: Do not start the engine during pushback.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.24 · DSC-31-15, PRO-NOR-SOP-07

q: What computes the GW and GW CG shown on the SD?
a: The FCMC, using the input ZFW and the actual position of the fuel.

q: Where are GW and GW CG displayed?
a: In green on the bottom right of the SD.

q: When is the GW CG displayed in red on the SD?
a: When the Flight Envelope portion of the FMGEC detects an out of limit CG.

q: What are the white messages under MAINTENANCE on the STATUS page?
a: Class 2 Maintenance messages, requiring no action by the flight crew.

q: What does the ECAM SWITCHING DMC knob select?
a: Which DMC supplies data to the E/WD and SD.

q: With ECAM SWITCHING in AUTO, which DMC takes over if DMC 3 fails?
a: DMC 1.

q: What does the ECAM/ND switch do?
a: Transfers the SD to either the Captains or First Officers ND.

q: What does the ECAM/ND switch transfer if both the E/WD and SD display units have failed?
a: The E/WD to the ND.

q: What does the EFIS DMC SWITCHING selector choose?
a: Which DMC supplies data to the respective PFD and ND.

q: What does the Engine position of the EFIS mode select switch display?
a: The engine portion of the E/WD on the ND.

q: What does the LS button display?
a: The localizer and glide slope scales on the PFD.

q: For which approaches is the LS button used?
a: Only approaches utilizing a localizer: ILS, LOC, LDA.

q: For which approaches must the LS button be off?
a: Approaches not utilizing a localizer: RNAV, VOR, NDB.

q: What can a Display Unit (DU) failure look like?
a: Blank screen with amber "Invalid Display Unit", blank screen with amber "F", or a distorted display.

q: Is a failed Display Unit recoverable?
a: No. The DU is not recoverable.

q: Which displays does DMC 1 provide data to?
a: The Captains PFD and ND.

q: Which displays does DMC 2 provide data to?
a: The First Officers PFD and ND.

q: Which displays does DMC 3 provide data to?
a: The E/WD and SD.

q: How does a DMC failure appear on the associated DUs?
a: "Invalid Data" in amber. The DUs can be recovered by switching DMC.

q: What happens if the E/WD DU fails?
a: The data automatically switches to the SD.

q: Does the SD automatically switch locations if its DU fails?
a: No.

q: How can SD data be displayed after the SD DU fails?
a: ECAM/ND XFR to the Captains or FOs ND, or press and hold a systems button over the E/WD.

q: Which DMCs can ECAM SWITCHING manually select as source for the E/WD and SD?
a: DMC 1 or 2.

q: What does the TO CONFIG Pb simulate?
a: The application of takeoff power, to test if the aircraft is configured for takeoff.

q: Which items does the TO CONFIG test check?
a: Slats/Flaps, Pitch Trim, Rudder Trim, Speed Brakes, Brake Temperatures, Doors.

q: Which two monitored items are not checked by the TO CONFIG test?
a: Parking Brake and Thrust not set.

q: What does EMER CANC do to a Warning?
a: Silences it while the failure continues and extinguishes Master Warning lights. The ECAM message remains.

q: What does EMER CANC do to a Caution?
a: Cancels it for the remainder of the flight and brings up the Status page showing "Cancelled Caution".

q: How is a cancelled Caution restored?
a: Hold RCL for more than 3 seconds.

q: In which cases would EMER CANC be used?
a: To move a MEL item ECAM off the Status page, or to cancel nuisance repeating on/off Cautions.

q: Which ECAM control panel keys are hardwired and still function if the panel fails?
a: CLR, STS, RCL, EMER CNCL, ALL.

q: When do the recorders start automatically?
a: On the ground for 5 minutes after power up, on the ground after first engine start, and in flight.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · DSC-31-60-10, DSC-23-10-40

q: How long do the recorders run automatically after power up on the ground?
a: 5 minutes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · DSC-31-60-10, DSC-23-10-40

q: What does the RCDR GND CTL Pb do?
a: Energizes the recorders during the preflight.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · DSC-31-60-10, DSC-23-10-40

q: Why is the CHRONO started at the beginning of the takeoff roll?
a: To allow monitoring of engine thrust limitations.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · PRO-NOR-SOP-12, LIM-ENG

q: What is the engine thrust time limit at 900° in normal operations?
a: 5 minutes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · PRO-NOR-SOP-12, LIM-ENG

q: What is the engine thrust time limit at 900° if an engine has failed?
a: 10 minutes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.27 · PRO-NOR-SOP-12, LIM-ENG

q: How is the landing gear normally controlled and operated?
a: Electrically controlled and hydraulically operated using the green hydraulic system.

q: How is the gear controlled and operated during gravity extension?
a: Electrically controlled and mechanically operated.

q: Can the gear be retracted normally after gravity extension if green pressure is available?
a: Yes. Retract by normal methods after resetting the gravity extension switch.

q: What must be done with the gravity extension switch before a normal retraction?
a: Move it to RESET, then to OFF.

q: How many Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIUs) control the gear system?
a: Two.

q: Which LGCIU powers the Landing Gear Indicator Panel next to the gear handle?
a: LGCIU 1.

q: What does red UNLK on the Landing Gear Indicator Panel mean?
a: The gear is not in the selected position.

q: What does a green triangle on the Landing Gear Indicator Panel mean?
a: The gear is down and locked.

q: Which LGCIUs power the two triangles per gear on the SD WHEEL page?
a: Left triangle LGCIU 1, right triangle LGCIU 2.

q: How many SD WHEEL page triangles per gear are needed to show down and locked?
a: Only one.

q: When does the Red Arrow next to the landing gear handle come on?
a: At 750 ft RA if the gear is not downlocked with Flaps 2, 3, or FULL.

q: What activates automatic braking?
a: Ground spoiler deployment.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.28 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: Below what speed will the autobrakes not engage during an RTO?
a: Below 72 kts, because the ground spoilers do not deploy until 72 kts.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.28 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: When do the autobrakes activate in LOW?
a: 1 second after the ground spoilers deploy, following gear touchdown with Thrust Levers IDLE.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.28 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: When do the autobrakes activate in MED?
a: When the ground spoilers deploy, following gear touchdown with Thrust Levers IDLE.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.28 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: When during taxi may the autobrakes be armed to MAX?
a: Only after the flight control check.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: Why not arm autobrakes MAX before the flight control check?
a: The rising spoilers during the check could activate the autobrakes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: What does the DECEL light on the autobrake Pbs mean?
a: Only that the aircraft is slowing at the programmed rate, not that the brakes are slowing it.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: What is the normal landing autobrake setting?
a: LOW.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: When should autobrakes MED be used?
a: For short or contaminated runways.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: When are autobrakes MAX used?
a: Only for takeoff.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-10, PRO-NOR-SOP-16

q: What is the normal position of the A/SKID and N/W STRG switch?
a: ON for normal operations.

q: Which hydraulic system powers the brakes when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
a: The Blue system, switched over from the Green system.

q: Is antiskid available with A/SKID and N/W STRG switched OFF?
a: No. Antiskid is deactivated.

q: What happens to nosewheel steering when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
a: Nosewheel steering is lost.

q: Where is braking pressure displayed when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
a: On the triple indicator.

q: What second function does the A/SKID and N/W STRG switch serve?
a: A computer reset. Check the QRH reset table on 02.02E.

q: How many different methods of braking does the aircraft have?
a: Four.

q: Which hydraulic system powers normal brakes?
a: The Green system.

q: Which hydraulic system powers alternate brakes, with or without A/SKID?
a: The Blue system.

q: What powers the Parking Brake?
a: The Blue system and the Accumulator.

q: What holds the aircraft when it is parked with the engines off?
a: Accumulator pressure.

q: Why is Engine 1 normally started first?
a: The Blue hydraulic pump is on Engine 1. It recharges the accumulator and pressurizes the parking brake.

q: What does the top scale of the triple indicator display?
a: Accumulator pressure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-04

q: What does the amber scale on the top of the triple indicator indicate?
a: The forbidden range. Recharge the accumulator using the blue hydraulic system.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-04

q: Where must accumulator pressure read during preflight to ensure the Parking Brake holds the aircraft?
a: In the green band.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-04

q: What does the bottom scale of the triple indicator display?
a: Blue system pressure delivered to the brakes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-04

q: What does the green band on the bottom scale of the triple indicator indicate?
a: The normal braking range.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.29 · DSC-32-30-20, PRO-NOR-SOP-04

q: What positions can the Parking Brake valve take?
a: Open or closed only, there is no in between.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: Is brake pedal pressure required to set the Parking Brake?
a: No. No pressure on the brake pedals is required.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: How long can the accumulator hold the Parking Brake?
a: 12 hours.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: What braking technique does the LOSS OF BRAKING memory item procedure call for?
a: Short and successive applications to stop the aircraft.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: How many full brake applications will the accumulator provide at least?
a: At least 7 full brake applications.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: Why delay braking to as low a speed as possible during a LOSS OF BRAKING?
a: To avoid tire burst.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-32-30-10, DSC-32-30-20

q: What does the ATT HDG switch allow?
a: IR 3 to replace IR 1 or IR 2.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What is lost when an IR fails?
a: Attitude and heading information as well as the map.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What does the AIR DATA switch allow?
a: ADR 3 to replace ADR 1 or ADR 2.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What data is lost when an ADR fails?
a: Airspeed and altitude data.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What does the FM switch allow?
a: Switching to the healthy FM in the event of FM failure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: How can NAVAIDS be tuned in Back up Navigation after both FMs fail?
a: Using the Nav function on the RMPs.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Which MCDU keys still function in Back up Navigation?
a: Only the corner keys (DIR, PROG, FPLN).
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: How must the crew navigate in Back up Navigation?
a: Use HDG/TRACK. NAV mode is inoperative.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Does the MCDU retain the flight plan after both FMs fail?
a: Yes. The MCDU continuously memorizes the flight plan.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Do the radios still function in Back up Navigation?
a: Yes. Radios still function normally.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What does the AUDIO switch allow?
a: The Captain or FO to utilize ACP 3 in case of ACP 1 or 2 failure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.30 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Which ADIRS rotary switch position is used for normal operations?
a: NAV.

q: What does the ADIRS rotary switch ATT position provide?
a: Only attitude and heading information.

q: How often must the heading be updated through the MCDU in ATT mode?
a: Every 10 minutes.

q: What does the ADIRS rotary switch OFF position do?
a: Shuts off the entire ADIRU (both IR and ADR).

q: How can the IR and ADR be turned off separately?
a: Using their associated Pb's.

q: What does a flashing IR fault indicate?
a: Attitude and heading information can be recovered in ATT mode.

q: What does a solid IR fault indicate?
a: The IR has failed.

q: How many types of ADIRS alignment are there?
a: Two, Quick Alignment and Full Alignment.

q: What does a Quick Alignment clear?
a: Only the groundspeed.

q: How long does a Quick Alignment take?
a: 30 seconds.

q: When is a Quick Alignment used?
a: When a full alignment is not required.

q: What does a Full Alignment clear?
a: Groundspeed and drift. It also captures present position.

q: How long does a Full Alignment take?
a: 7 to 10 minutes.

q: Why are the ADIRS left on when leaving the aircraft?
a: They provide fuel system information to calculate fuel density during fueling.

q: Is an ADIRS alignment during preflight acceptable while fueling?
a: Yes. It is the normal procedure.

q: With IRS only navigation in RNP 10 airspace, what is the time limit from the IRS ground alignment?
a: Less than 6.2 hours outside radio navaid coverage.

q: With IRS only navigation in RNP 10 airspace, what is the time limit from the last FM position update?
a: Less than 5.7 hours outside radio navaid coverage.

q: Why does the ON BAT light illuminate momentarily when turning the ADIRS on?
a: It is an internal power check using the aircraft batteries.

q: What indicates the ADIRS are using the aircraft batteries for power?
a: A horn sounds in the nose wheel well, the same horn as the APU fire horn.

q: What is the Mix IRS position?
a: Each FMGEC's average of the 3 IRS provided positions.

q: How does the Mix IRS treat one IRS position with a dramatic difference?
a: It is factored in less than the other two.

q: What is the bias in the GPIRS position computation?
a: The difference between the MIX IRS position and the GPIRS position, compared by each FMGEC.

q: How does the system handle the bias?
a: It is constantly memorized by the system.

q: What does the system do if radio or GPIRS data is lost?
a: Adjusts the MIX IRS position using the bias and navigates on it until data is restored.

q: Which IR can replace IR 1 or IR 2 using the ATT HDG switch?
a: IR 3.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.32 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Which ADR can replace ADR 1 or ADR 2 using the AIR DATA switch?
a: ADR 3.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.32 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Is NAV mode available in Back up Navigation after both FMs fail?
a: No. NAV mode is inoperative, use HDG/TRACK to navigate.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: Which ACP does the AUDIO switch give the Captain or FO?
a: ACP 3, in case of ACP 1 or 2 failure.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-34-10-10, DSC-22-10-10, DSC-23-10-50

q: What does GPWS SYS Off inhibit?
a: Basic GPWS Modes 1-5. It does not affect the terrain function.

q: What information does the GPWS TERR function use?
a: Database terrain information, operating independently of the Basic modes 1-5.

q: When would TERR be selected off?
a: Due to NOTAM, or runway/airport not in the database.

q: When should GPWS G/S Mode be turned off?
a: Only due to a failure, glideslope signal unreliable.

q: When should GPWS Flap Mode be turned off?
a: Only during failures requiring landing with Flaps 0-2.

q: Why is Flap Mode off not required for a single engine landing?
a: FLAPS 3 can be selected on the MCDU.

q: What does the PULL UP/GPWS Pb on the forward panel do?
a: Temporarily inhibits the glideslope MODE 5 alert.

q: What action is required if LOW OIL LEVEL is displayed on the APU SD page before a ground start?
a: Advise Maintenance.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: How long can the APU operate after LOW OIL LEVEL is displayed?
a: 15 hours.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the APU starter limit?
a: 3 starts then a 60-minute cooldown.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: Can APU bleed be used for Wing Anti-Ice?
a: No. It is not permitted.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the APU start limit altitude?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the maximum altitude for an APU start using batteries?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use plus APU bleed for 1 pack?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the maximum altitude for engine start using APU bleed?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use plus APU bleed for 2 packs?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.33 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: From where can the APU be shut down outside the aircraft?
a: Two locations, the Refueling Panel and the External Power Panel.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What controls all the APU logic?
a: The Electronic Control Box (ECB).
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What does an APU MASTER Switch Fault mean?
a: An automatic shutdown has occurred.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What does resetting the APU MASTER Switch reset?
a: The ECB.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What happens when the APU MASTER Switch is selected ON?
a: The APU page is called on the SD and the APU intake flap opens.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: When does the APU START switch engage the starter?
a: When the air intake is fully open with the Master Switch ON.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What does the APU AVAIL light mean?
a: The APU is available for Electric and/or Air.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: From which 3 places is the APU supplied fuel through the trim tank transfer line?
a: Left Inner Collector Tank, Trim Pipe, Trim Tank, depending on phase of flight.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What must be maintained in the trim tank transfer line for the APU to function?
a: Fuel.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: How is the APU shut down from the cockpit panel?
a: Turn the MASTER Switch off.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What does the AVAIL light do during APU cool down?
a: It remains on.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: How long can APU cool down take after the MASTER Switch is turned off?
a: Up to 2 minutes.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: When does the ECB command an automatic APU shutdown in the air?
a: Overspeed and certain critical ECB failures.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: In the air, what causes the ECB to command an automatic APU shutdown?
a: Overspeed and certain critical ECB failures.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.34 · DSC-49-20, LIM-APU

q: What is the active range of the Autothrust in normal operations?
a: From IDLE to CLIMB detents.

q: What is the active range of the Autothrust in single engine operations?
a: From IDLE to MCT detents.

q: What does MAN START provide?
a: An alternate method of engine start.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.35 · DSC-70-80-30, PRO-NOR-SUP-ENG

q: What should pilots follow when a Manual Start is required?
a: The Supplementary Procedures.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.35 · DSC-70-80-30, PRO-NOR-SUP-ENG

q: Are Start Fault protections available during a Manual Start?
a: No. The pilots must manually abort a start if there is an issue.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.35 · DSC-70-80-30, PRO-NOR-SUP-ENG

q: When is N1 Rated or N1 Degraded mode triggered?
a: When EPR cannot be computed by the FADEC.

q: What determines whether N1 Rated or N1 Degraded mode is triggered?
a: Which inputs to the FADEC have failed.

q: What do the N1 Mode Pb's allow if only one engine is affected?
a: Both engines selected to N1 mode to maintain similar thrust settings.

q: What parameter controls the engine when N1 Mode is active?
a: N1, not EPR.

q: Is A/THR available when N1 Mode is active?
a: No. It is lost but can be regained if only one engine is in degraded mode.

q: When is Alpha Floor lost in N1 Mode?
a: When both engines are in degraded mode.

q: Are Flex takeoffs allowed when dispatched in N1 mode?
a: No. Flex takeoffs are prohibited.

q: How many levels of N1 mode are there?
a: Two, N1 Rated Mode and N1 Degraded Mode.

q: What does the FADEC display in N1 Rated Mode?
a: N1 limits on the upper right of the E/WD. Normal engine protections still provided.

q: What limits are provided in N1 Degraded Mode?
a: None on the E/WD. The FADEC computes a N1 red line.

q: What does the N1 Degraded Mode red line represent?
a: The full forward position of the Thrust Lever.

q: Is the N1 Degraded Mode red line within the actual N1 limit?
a: No. It is beyond the actual N1 limit and can also exceed EGT limits.

q: With one engine in degraded mode, what does selecting the other engine's N1 Mode Pb do?
a: Puts it in rated mode. The displayed rated mode limits can be used for both engines.

q: Which chart is used when operating in N1 Degraded Mode?
a: The N1 Mode Thrust Control chart in the FCOM (PER-THR-N1).

q: What does the Engine Master Switch initiate with the ENG START selector at IGN/START?
a: The automatic start sequence.

q: What must be set before the Engine Master Switch initiates a manual start sequence?
a: ENG START selector at IGN/START and ENG MAN START Pb selected ON.

q: What three effects does selecting IGN/START on the ENG START selector have?
a: Brings up the Engine page on the SD, powers the FADEC, closes the Pack Flow Control Valves.

q: What happens to the Pack Flow Control Valves when IGN/START is selected?
a: They close.

q: What does FADEC stand for?
a: Full Authority Digital Engine Control.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: How many Pbs on the Maintenance Panel provide power to the FADECs on the ground?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: Besides the Maintenance Panel Pbs, what else powers the FADECs?
a: Selecting IGN/START on the ENG START selector.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: What happens to the Pack valves when FADECs are powered by IGN/START?
a: They close, then reopen when selected back to NORM.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: Why are the FADECs energized during preflight?
a: To check the Engine oil level.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: What is the minimum engine oil quantity required?
a: 15 qts, or 6 qts plus estimated consumption (0.7 qt/h), whichever is higher.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: What engine oil consumption rate is used for the estimate?
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20

q: Do the FADECs rely on aircraft power to continue operating?
a: No. They have their own magnetic alternators.
src: REV1 Systems Guide p.36 · DSC-70-20, DSC-29-20
